exams.title: 2026 Term 3 Quiz 1
exams.description: Comprehensive mock exam covering HTML, CSS, and JS.

questions.title: The four rules below all set the colour of the same button.

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: What colour is the button text, and how does the browser choose between the four rules? Explain what it compares and why source order does not decide the result here.
subQuestions.answerMdx:
The button text is GREEN.
ID always takes precedent over classes and type selectors.
The order does not matter unless it's two tied things (e.g. .important and button.important)
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for identifying the text as green.
1 mark for explaining about precedent
1 mark for highlighting order only matters with a tie

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The student cannot change the id rule, so they add !important to the first rule. What colour is the text now?
subQuestions.answerMdx: The button text becomes BLUE.
subQuestions.markingMdx: 1 mark for identifying the text as blue.

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Why does routinely using !important cause problems? Describe what a developer should usually do when a rule is not taking effect.
subQuestions.answerMdx:
It ends the conversation. Once a declaration is important, the only ways to override
it are another !important or an inline style, so the next person with a legitimate
reason to change that colour has to escalate too. Stylesheets that use it accumulate
!important on top of !important until specificity no longer means anything and the
cascade cannot be reasoned about at all.

If a rule is not taking effect, the developer should inspect the element in the
browser dev tools, check which rule is winning in the cascade, and then fix the
normal CSS by changing the selector, specificity, or source order instead of
adding !important as a shortcut.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining one real problem caused by routinely using `!important`.
1 mark for describing what to do instead, including diagnosing with dev tools or
fixing the selector rather than just "try harder".

questions.title: A badge is positioned over a photo.

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The badge is positioned 20px from the hero's right edge. How many pixels from the hero's left edge is the badge's left edge? Show where the hero's width comes from and why it is needed for the calculation.
subQuestions.answerMdx:
300px.

right: 20px pins the badge's RIGHT edge 20px in from the hero's right edge, and
the badge is 80px wide, so its left edge sits at:

  400 - 20 - 80 = 300px
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for calculating the badge's left edge as 300px.
1 mark for explaining it.

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The developer removes position relative from the hero. Where does the badge move, and what are top and right now measured against?
subQuestions.answerMdx:
The badge ends up in the top right corner of the page — 20px from the top and
20px from the right of the window — rather than in the corner of the hero. Absolute will
attach to the nearest previous relative.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating where the badge moves: the top right of the page or viewport.
1 mark for explaining that the offsets are measured from the nearest positioned
ancestor, or from the initial containing block when there is none.

questions.title: Determine the size and spacing of the two blocks below. Each element has its natural height unless a height is specified, and the page is wider than 600px.

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Calculate the card's total width in pixels, showing your working. Then state its total width if box-sizing were set to border-box.
subQuestions.answerMdx:
444px.

width: 400px sets the CONTENT box, because box-sizing defaults to content-box.
The padding and the border are then added outside it:

  400 (content) + 20 + 20 (padding) + 2 + 2 (border) = 444px
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for calculating 444px
1 mark for working shown.

questions.title: A website remembers whether the user chose dark mode.

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: A user visits the site for the first time. What does `localStorage.getItem('theme')` return, and is the page shown in dark mode?
subQuestions.answerMdx:
It returns null, because nothing has been saved under 'theme' yet.
The if condition is false, so the page is NOT in dark mode.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating getItem returns null.
1 mark for stating the page is not in dark mode.

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The user clicks the button, closes the browser, and comes back the next day. Is the page in dark mode? Explain why.
subQuestions.answerMdx:
Yes, the page is in dark mode.
setItem saved 'dark' in localStorage, which stays in the browser even after it
is closed. When the page loads, getItem returns 'dark' and the class is added.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating the page is in dark mode.
1 mark for explaining that localStorage keeps data after the browser is closed.

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The developer deletes the `localStorage.setItem` line. What happens now when the user clicks the button and then reloads the page?
subQuestions.answerMdx:
Clicking still turns the page dark, but after reloading it goes back to light.
Without setItem the choice is never saved, so getItem returns null on reload.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating the page goes back to light mode after reloading.
1 mark for explaining that the choice is no longer saved to localStorage.

questions.title: A button shows a message when it is clicked.

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: What does the user see when the page first loads, and what happens when they click the button?
subQuestions.answerMdx:
When the page loads the paragraph is empty, so no message is shown.
When the button is clicked, showMessage runs and "Hello!" appears in the paragraph.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating no message is shown on load.
1 mark for stating "Hello!" appears when the button is clicked.

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The developer changes the last line to `button.addEventListener('click', showMessage());`. What happens now, and why?
subQuestions.answerMdx:
"Hello!" appears straight away when the page loads, without any click.
The brackets call showMessage immediately instead of passing the function to
addEventListener, so it is not run when the button is clicked.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating the message appears immediately on page load.
1 mark for explaining that the brackets call the function straight away.

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The developer changes `'click'` to `'mouseover'`. When does the message appear now?
subQuestions.answerMdx:
The message appears when the user moves their mouse over the button, without
needing to click it. The event name decides which user action runs the function.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating the message appears when the mouse moves over the button.
1 mark for explaining that the event name controls when the function runs.

questions.title: A sign-up form shows a welcome message.

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The user types `Sam` into the box and clicks Sign up. What is shown on the page? Explain where the name comes from.
subQuestions.answerMdx:
"Welcome, Sam" is shown in the paragraph.
.value reads the text the user typed into the input box.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating "Welcome, Sam".
1 mark for explaining that .value gives the text typed into the input.

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The developer deletes the `event.preventDefault();` line. What happens now when the form is submitted?
subQuestions.answerMdx:
The browser submits the form the normal way and reloads the page, so the
welcome message disappears straight away (or is never seen).
preventDefault is what stops the browser's default submit behaviour.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating the page reloads and the message disappears.
1 mark for explaining that preventDefault stops the default form submission.

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The developer wants to stop the form from being submitted when the name box is empty, without writing any JavaScript. What should they add to the HTML, and what happens if the user then clicks Sign up with the box empty?
subQuestions.answerMdx:
Add the required attribute to the input:

  <input id="name" type="text" required>

The browser then stops the form from submitting and shows a message asking the
user to fill in the field, so no welcome message is shown.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for adding the required attribute to the input.
1 mark for stating the browser blocks the submission and shows a warning.

questions.title: A page changes its layout on small screens.

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The page is viewed on a laptop with a screen 1000px wide. What size is the title, and is the menu shown? Explain why.
subQuestions.answerMdx:
The title is 32px and the menu is shown.
The screen is wider than 600px, so the rules inside the media query do not apply.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating 32px and the menu is shown.
1 mark for explaining the media query does not apply above 600px.

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The page is viewed on a phone with a screen 400px wide. What size is the title, and is the menu shown? Explain why.
subQuestions.answerMdx:
The title is 20px and the menu is hidden.
The screen is 600px or narrower, so the rules inside the media query apply and
override the earlier rules.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating 20px and the menu is hidden.
1 mark for explaining the media query applies at 600px or below.

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: What is the purpose of the `<meta name="viewport">` tag in the head?
subQuestions.answerMdx:
It tells the phone to use its real screen width for the page instead of
pretending to be a wide desktop screen and zooming out. Without it, the phone
may not match max-width: 600px, so the mobile styles would not apply.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining it makes the page use the device's real width.
1 mark for explaining that without it the mobile styles may not apply.

questions.title: A simple web page about a trip.
questions.contentMdx:
``` My Trip

Trip to Sydney

  • Opera House
  • Harbour Bridge
```

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Where does the text "My Trip" appear, and where does "Trip to Sydney" appear?
subQuestions.answerMdx:
"My Trip" appears in the browser tab, because it is inside <title> in the head.
"Trip to Sydney" appears on the page itself as the main heading, because it is
inside <h1> in the body.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating "My Trip" appears in the browser tab.
1 mark for stating "Trip to Sydney" appears on the page as a heading.

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The developer wants the list to be numbered 1, 2 instead of using bullet points. What should they change?
subQuestions.answerMdx:
Change
    to
      (and
to ). ul is an unordered list shown with bullets; ol is an ordered list shown with numbers.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for changing ul to ol.
1 mark for explaining the difference between unordered and ordered lists.

questions.title: A student uses browser dev tools to work out why their page is broken.

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The student selects a heading in the Elements panel. In the Styles pane, their rule `color: red` is shown with a line through it. What does the line mean, and how can they find out which rule is actually setting the colour?
subQuestions.answerMdx:
The line means the declaration matched the element but was overridden by
another rule, for example one with higher specificity or one that comes later.
They can look for the rule higher up in the Styles pane that is not crossed out,
or open the Computed tab to see the final colour and which rule it came from.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining that the rule was overridden by another rule.
1 mark for describing how to find the winning rule (Styles pane or Computed tab).

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The student fixes the colour by editing it directly in the Styles pane, and the page looks right. When they reload the page, the fix is gone. Why, and what should they do?
subQuestions.answerMdx:
Changes made in dev tools only affect the copy of the page currently open in
the browser. They are not saved to the student's CSS file, so reloading loads
the original file again. They need to make the same change in their CSS file
and save it.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining dev tools edits are not saved to the source files.
1 mark for stating the change must be copied into the actual CSS file.

questions.title: A developer chooses image formats for a website.
questions.contentMdx:
The site needs three images:

- a large photo of a beach at sunset
- the company logo, with a transparent background, which must stay sharp at any size
- a small animated loading icon

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Choose the most suitable format for each image from JPG, PNG, GIF and SVG. Give a reason for each choice.
subQuestions.answerMdx:
Beach photo: JPG. It uses lossy compression, which keeps photos with lots of
colours and detail at a small file size.

Logo: SVG. It is a vector format, so it stays sharp at any size, and it supports
transparency.

Loading icon: GIF. It supports simple animation.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for each correct format with a valid reason.
Accept PNG for the logo only if transparency is mentioned (but it will not
scale sharply). Accept SVG or WebP for the loading icon if animation is mentioned.

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: The developer saves the beach photo as a PNG instead, and the file is about five times bigger. It also looks no better. Explain why.
subQuestions.answerMdx:
PNG is lossless, so it keeps every pixel exactly. A photo has lots of fine
detail and colour changes, which lossless compression cannot shrink well.
JPG throws away detail the eye barely notices, so it is much smaller while
looking almost the same.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining PNG is lossless and keeps all the detail.
1 mark for explaining JPG discards detail people do not notice, making it smaller.

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: Someone saves the logo as a JPG instead. On the site's dark blue header it now has a white box around it, and it looks blurry when shown larger. Explain both problems.
subQuestions.answerMdx:
White box: JPG does not support transparency, so the transparent background
is filled in with a solid colour (white).

Blurry: JPG is a raster format made of a fixed number of pixels. Showing it
larger stretches those pixels, so it looks blurry or blocky. An SVG is
drawn from shapes, so it can be redrawn sharply at any size.
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining JPG has no transparency.
1 mark for explaining raster images blur when scaled up, unlike vector images.

exams.title: Week 1 模拟试卷
exams.description: Week 1 知识点模拟试卷：覆盖 Git 最小工作流、HTML 文档结构、语义化标签、链接图片路径与列表表格代码标签五条主线。

questions.title: Git 最小工作流
questions.contentMdx:
```bash
git clone <repo-url>
# 修改 index.html
git add index.html
git commit -m "add hero section"
git push
```

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: 上面的命令序列里，`git add` 和 `git commit` 分别完成了什么？为什么两者要分开执行，而不是合并成一步？
subQuestions.answerMdx: `git add` 把工作区的改动登记到暂存区（staging area），决定“哪些改动要进入这次提交”；`git commit` 把暂存区里的内容固化成一条历史记录。分开是因为一次提交往往只应包含一组相关改动，先 `add` 让你有机会挑选要提交的文件，而不是把所有改动一把提交。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for describing add as staging changes.
1 mark for describing commit as recording the staged snapshot, and why staging is a separate step.

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: 如果开发者跳过 `git commit` 直接执行 `git push`，远端仓库会发生什么？
subQuestions.answerMdx: 远端不会有任何变化。`git push` 只是把本地已经存在的提交推送到远端；如果本地没有新的 commit，就没有东西可以推。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating the remote does not change.
1 mark for explaining that push only sends existing local commits.

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: 为什么在 `git add` 之前通常先执行 `git diff`？它解决了什么问题？
subQuestions.answerMdx: `git diff` 让你在提交前复查工作区相对上次提交到底改了什么，避免把调试代码、临时改动或误删一起提交进去。它是提交前的自检手段。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating that git diff previews unstaged changes.
1 mark for explaining it prevents committing unintended changes.

questions.title: HTML 文档结构
questions.contentMdx:
```html My Trip

Trip to Sydney

```

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: 第一行的 `<!DOCTYPE html>` 有什么作用？如果把它删掉，浏览器会怎么处理这个页面？
subQuestions.answerMdx: 它告诉浏览器使用标准模式（standards mode）渲染页面。删掉后浏览器可能退回怪异模式（quirks mode），导致盒模型计算、排版等行为与预期不一致。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for identifying the standard rendering mode.
1 mark for mentioning quirks mode or inconsistent rendering without it.

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: 这段代码里的 "My Trip" 和 "Trip to Sydney" 分别显示在哪里？
subQuestions.answerMdx: "My Trip" 显示在浏览器标签页（窗口标题）上，因为它位于 `<head>` 里的 `<title>` 中；"Trip to Sydney" 显示在页面正文里，因为它是 `<body>` 中的 `<h1>`。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for placing "My Trip" in the browser tab.
1 mark for placing "Trip to Sydney" in the page body.

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: `<head>` 和 `<body>` 各自承载什么内容？为什么 `<title>` 不能放在 `<body>` 里？
subQuestions.answerMdx: `<head>` 放页面的元信息，例如 `<title>`、`<meta>`、样式表和脚本引用，这些不会直接显示为正文；`<body>` 放用户在页面上能看到的所有内容。`<title>` 属于元信息，所以必须放在 `<head>`，放在 `<body>` 里既不符合规范也不会被当作页面标题处理。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for contrasting metadata (head) with visible content (body).
1 mark for explaining why title belongs to head.

subQuestions.label: (d)
subQuestions.questionMdx: `<html lang="en">` 中 `lang` 属性的意义是什么？
subQuestions.answerMdx: 它声明了文档的主要语言，帮助屏幕阅读器用正确的语音朗读，也让浏览器翻译、拼写检查与搜索引擎更好地理解内容。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for identifying document language declaration.
1 mark for mentioning accessibility or translation/SEO benefits.

questions.title: 语义化标签与标题层级
questions.contentMdx:
```html
Course App
Home
Learning HTML
HTML is the foundation of the web.
```

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: 上面这段代码被称为 "div soup"。请用合适的语义化标签重构顶层结构（导航区和主内容区）。
subQuestions.answerMdx:
```html
Course App
Home

Learning HTML

HTML is the foundation of the web.

```
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for using header/nav for the top area.
1 mark for using main/article and h1/p for the content area.

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: 使用语义化标签相比全部用 `<div>` 更好，请给出至少两个原因。
subQuestions.answerMdx:
1. 可访问性（A11Y）：屏幕阅读器能识别页面结构，帮助视障用户跳转和导航。
2. SEO：搜索引擎能更好理解内容层次与重点。
3. 可读性：开发者不必完全依赖 class 命名就能看懂结构。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for accessibility or screen readers.
1 mark for SEO or developer readability.

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: `<h1>` 到 `<h6>` 表达的是视觉大小还是结构层级？一个页面通常应该有几个 `<h1>`？
subQuestions.answerMdx: 表达的是结构层级（标题的重要性与从属关系），而不是视觉大小；视觉大小应交给 CSS 控制。一个页面通常只应有一个 `<h1>` 作为主标题。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating h1-h6 express structural hierarchy, not visual size.
1 mark for stating a page should normally have a single h1.

subQuestions.label: (d)
subQuestions.questionMdx: 什么情况下应该继续使用 `<div>` / `<span>`，而不是强行套语义标签？
subQuestions.answerMdx: 当这一段内容只是出于布局或样式的需要，本身没有独立语义（例如单纯的分组容器），且没有更合适的语义标签时，用 `<div>` 做块级分组、`<span>` 做行内分组是合适的。语义标签要用在真正表达结构的地方，滥用反而会误导辅助技术。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining div/span as neutral containers for styling or layout.
1 mark for warning against misusing semantic tags where no semantics exist.

questions.title: 链接、图片与路径
questions.contentMdx: ```html About ``` 假设页面本身位于 `/pages/detail.html`。

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: `src="images/logo.png"` 与 `src="/images/logo.png"` 有什么区别？在上面的页面地址下，两者分别会请求哪个路径？
subQuestions.answerMdx: `images/logo.png` 是相对路径，相对于当前页面所在目录解析，会请求 `/pages/images/logo.png`；`/images/logo.png` 是根路径，相对于站点根目录解析，会请求 `/images/logo.png`。前者容易在页面移动到别的目录后失效。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for distinguishing relative vs root-relative resolution.
1 mark for giving the correct resolved paths or the fragility of relative paths.

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: `alt` 属性的作用是什么？请给出两个场景。
subQuestions.answerMdx: `alt` 提供图片的替代文本。1) 图片加载失败时浏览器显示这段文字；2) 屏幕阅读器读出它，让视障用户理解图片内容。它也是搜索引擎理解图片的依据。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for accessibility / screen reader usage.
1 mark for fallback when the image fails to load, or SEO.

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: 站点需要一张真实风景照片和一个线条风格的 logo。分别更适合用哪种图片格式？各说明理由。
subQuestions.answerMdx: 风景照片适合 JPG：它是有损压缩，能在保持观感的同时大幅减小照片体积。线条 logo 适合 SVG：它是矢量格式，任意缩放都不失真，通常体积小，并且可用 CSS/JS 修改样式。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for JPG for photos with a valid reason.
1 mark for SVG for a logo with a valid reason.

subQuestions.label: (d)
subQuestions.questionMdx: 如果开发者把 `src` 写成自己电脑上的绝对文件路径（例如 `/Users/sam/project/logo.png`），部署上线后会出现什么问题？为什么？
subQuestions.answerMdx: 其他访客的浏览器里没有这个本地文件路径，图片会加载失败。网页里的资源路径应使用相对于站点根目录或当前文档的路径，而不是本机文件系统路径，因为服务器与用户机器上的文件结构完全不同。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for stating the image breaks for other users.
1 mark for explaining that local filesystem paths do not exist on the server or client.

questions.title: 列表、表格与预格式化文本

subQuestions.label: (a)
subQuestions.questionMdx: `<ul>` 和 `<ol>` 有什么区别？想把上面的地点列表改成带编号的 1、2，应该改什么？
subQuestions.answerMdx:
`
    ` 是无序列表，用圆点等符号展示，各条目没有先后顺序；`
      ` 是有序列表，用数字编号展示，条目顺序有意义。把 `
        ` 改成 `
          `（结尾的 `
      ` 改成 `
    `）即可。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for distinguishing unordered vs ordered semantics.
1 mark for changing ul to ol.

subQuestions.label: (b)
subQuestions.questionMdx: 上面的表格里，`<thead>` / `<tbody>` / `<th>` / `<td>` 分别承担什么职责？
subQuestions.answerMdx: `<thead>` 是表头区域，`<tbody>` 是表体区域，用于把表头行和数据行分组；`<th>` 是表头单元格，语义上是列的标题；`<td>` 是普通数据单元格。它们的区分让辅助技术能正确理解表格的行列关系。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for explaining thead/tbody grouping.
1 mark for explaining th (header cell) vs td (data cell).

subQuestions.label: (c)
subQuestions.questionMdx: `<pre>` 和 `<code>` 的区别是什么？为什么展示代码时常把两者一起用？
subQuestions.answerMdx: `<code>` 只是语义上表示“这是一段代码”，本身不会保留空格和换行；`<pre>` 会保留原文的空白和换行。把 `<code>` 放进 `<pre>` 里，既声明了内容是代码，又保留了代码的缩进与换行格式。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for code as semantic marker and pre as preserving whitespace.
1 mark for explaining the combined use.

subQuestions.label: (d)
subQuestions.questionMdx: 什么时候适合用 `<table>` 展示数据，而不是用 flex/grid 去拼一个“看起来像表格”的布局？
subQuestions.answerMdx: 当内容本质上是“行与列的二维数据”（如城市与人口、课程与分数）时，应该用 `<table>`，因为它带有行列语义，便于屏幕阅读器理解；flex/grid 只负责视觉布局，不提供数据语义。反过来，仅为了排版对齐而用 `<table>` 也是不推荐的。
subQuestions.markingMdx:
1 mark for using table when content is genuinely tabular data.
1 mark for noting flex/grid offer layout but no data semantics.
